transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (Elmwood CTO), Mark (Elmwood Security Eng), Alex (Elmwood PM)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focusing on SSO test progress, audit log access/export, and retention policy decisions. Action items around SOC2 docs, KMS notes, and a small in-prod smoke test.

Topics: SSO/SAML test, audit logs and schema, data retention window, SOC 2 evidence, KMS/HSM integration, next pilot steps (smoke test / dedicated capacity).

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for carving time today, quick check-in on the pilot security items — i can kick off, real short agenda: sso, logs, retention, soc two docs, then liam will go over the log export mechanics. sound good?
[00:12] Priya (Elmwood): yes sounds good, we had the SSO test earlier and hit a couple of glitches so would like to prioritize that.
[00:18] Mark (Elmwood Sec): yeah the big ask for us is we need to ensure we can get audit logs out to our SIEM and we need a clear retention policy — legal wants 90 days but security prefers 30 with longer archival.
[00:30] Liam (Redwood SE): quick note — the SSO flow we walked through uses SAML 2.0 post binding, we saw the transient assertion expiring on our first run, which was a config issue on the IdP side (clock skew). that should be fixed if you push the NTP sync, but we can also extend the assertion lifetime on the Redwood side for the pilot.
[01:05] Alex (Elmwood PM): Mark, is the 90 days hard constraint or negotiable? legal said 90 but engineering pushed back on cost.
[01:12] Mark (Elmwood Sec): negotiable, but must be auditable; whatever we do we need tamper-evident logs and a way to prove chain of custody.
[01:27] Maya (Redwood AE): understood — from Redwood we offer two things: audit-log streaming (syslog / S3 / bigquery) and exported deltas. we also have built-in immutable logs for the control plane that are SOC2 covered. i'll attach the attestation.
[01:44] Priya: can you confirm where logs are stored and whether they include prompts/response payloads? that's a blocker for us re: pii exposure.
[01:53] Liam: short answer: by default for hosted we retain request/response for 30 days for pilot metrics and debugging, but we can configure field-level redaction and we offer private deployment options where you control persistence. also we support tokenization at ingress and sending only embeddings out.
[02:20] Mark: what about KMS — we need customer-managed key option, not just provider-managed.
[02:28] Maya: yes, KMS integration is available for Private and Dedicated customers; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with user-managed keys via our KMS proxy. i'll share the KMS integration guide.
[02:40] Speaker 6: (inaudible)
[02:47] Liam: quick demo note — audit logs come in two streams: control-plane events (deploys, rollouts, auth events) and data-plane events (request metadata, latency, errors). full payload retention is opt-in and can be disabled or scrubbed at the field level.
[03:10] Alex: scrubbing — can we redact email addresses and ssns before they hit storage? we prefer redaction pre-ingest.
[03:18] Liam: yes you can use our pre-processing webhook to scrub fields, or you can perform client-side tokenization. pre-ingest webhook is easiest for POC — it runs inline and returns cleaned input to the runtime.
[03:42] Priya: regarding SOC 2, do you have a full report or only a summary? our compliance team wants the full Type II.
[03:50] Maya: we can provide SOC 2 Type II for the control plane and attestations; the full report is shared under NDA — i'll start the exchange, should be able to send redacted controls matrix by friday.
[04:05] Mark: how do you demonstrate immutability? we need tamper evidence for logs for audits.
[04:13] Liam: logs are append-only and backed by a write-once store in our infra; we can also provide signed digests on a daily cadence for tamper evidence. if you push logs to your S3 bucket, you can enforce S3 object lock for retention.
[04:34] Priya: EU data residency — we have EU customers, so we need to ensure data at rest is in EU for EU-located users. can we scope the pilot to eu region?
[04:44] Maya: yes, region pinning is supported for Dedicated and for hosted we can route EU traffic to the eu-region cluster — for the pilot we can route your test traffic to the eu-region. note that audit exports to your SIEM must be configured to remain in-region if that's a hard requirement.
[05:05] Alex: about SSO testing — we gave you our IdP metadata (okta) and we saw an assertion error, are you expecting anything else for our next test?
[05:15] Liam: we need the entityID + the certificate bundle, and if possible a test user account with the email attribute in the assertion. we'll provide a short checklist in the ticket.
[05:34] Maya: i'll include that checklist and a staging runbook.
[05:38] Mark: what's your default log retention in hosted? you mentioned 30 days, but is that configurable?
[05:45] Liam: yes it's configurable per-tenant for hosted up to 90 days, beyond that we typically advise archival to customer S3 for cost and compliance. retention config is live in the console or via API.
[06:02] Priya: any charge implications if we increase retention to 90? need a rough estimate.
[06:08] Maya: yes there's storage cost — i'll include a back-of-envelope estimate in the follow-up (per GB/month and egress for exports).
[06:15] Alex: for the POC success criteria, what do we need to validate this week?
[06:21] Maya: SSO working end-to-end with two test users; audit log streaming into Elmwood SIEM with sample entries; confirmation of retention window and KMS approach. if all cleared we schedule a small smoke test on a dedicated pool.
[06:40] Mark: technically we'd like the logs to contain request-id, timestamp, model-id, route, and redaction flag. does your schema include request-id?
[06:48] Liam: yes schema includes request_id, trace_id, model_variant, latency_ms, and a redact_mask field. i'll attach the schema in the ticket.
[07:05] Priya: about PII — is it possible to store only embeddings and not retain the original text at all?
[07:12] Liam: yes you can pre-tokenize or use transform to embeddings and then store just the embeddings; note that embeddings can still be considered sensitive but they're smaller and easier to pseudonymize.
[07:30] Alex: any legal language around deletion we should be aware of? e.g., can you guarantee deletion within X hours of a request?
[07:38] Maya: deletion requests are supported; for hosted we typically process deletion scrub within 48-72 hours for request/response caches and immediate removal from accessible indexes; deep archival scrub can take longer depending on retention and backups — we'll detail this in the follow-up.
[07:59] Mark: for audit purposes we also need exportable logs with signed timestamps. you mentioned daily digests — can we get a sample digest file?
[08:08] Liam: yes sample digest available, i will upload the sample .sig + .ndjson example.
[08:20] Speaker 6: (mumbled)
[08:30] Priya: one more item — we have regulated customers in healthcare; would Redwood accept a BAA?
[08:38] Maya: we have customers in regulated spaces; we can discuss BAA under our enterprise contract — i'll loop in legal once we get to contracting.
[08:48] Alex: operational question: for smoke test on 9/22, what's involvement expected from our side?
[08:55] Maya: minimal — one test user to run test prompts, security to validate audit records, and engineering to confirm SSO flows. we will do the heavy lifting for infra.
[09:10] Mark: can you confirm where audit logs are accessible — via console, API, or streaming only?
[09:18] Liam: accessible all three ways — console for browsing, API for query, and streaming for SIEM ingest. streaming supports syslog and HTTPS webhooks.
[09:32] Priya: will you expose who accessed which logs? need RBAC and fine-grained audit.
[09:40] Liam: RBAC is supported; role bindings map to read/write/export permissions and every access is itself logged in the control-plane audit.
[09:55] Alex: quick thought — for cost reasons we might want to only retain control-plane logs long-term and scrub data-plane payloads. is that a pattern others use?
[10:02] Maya: yes that's common — keep control-plane for 365+ days, data-plane short-term. we'll show a recommended retention config for your use-case.
[10:20] Mark: any risk with using customer KMS for keys — does Redwood ever see plaintext keys?
[10:27] Liam: no, with customer-managed keys via KMS we perform envelope encryption — Redwood never stores customer plaintext key materials; we hold only the encrypted DEKs. for HSM we can do additional attestation.
[10:45] Priya: ok that's reassuring.
[10:50] Maya: let's go through a short run-through of the SSO checklist now — Liam, can you pull up the checklist?
[10:58] Liam: sure — checklist items: idp metadata, x509 cert, entity id, assertion attribute mapping (email/name), test user credentials, clock sync. i've posted the checklist link in the chat.
[11:18] Alex: noted, we'll share the test user by EOD.
[11:22] Priya: regarding exports to our SIEM, do you support CEF format or only JSON/ndjson?
[11:30] Liam: currently JSON/NDJSON natively, but we can do CEF conversion in the export pipeline if needed — it's a small mapping.
[11:40] Mark: how do you handle deletion requests that intersect with legal hold? for audits we might have holds that prevent deletion.
[11:50] Maya: legal hold supersedes deletion requests; we keep an audit trail of holds and can toggle retention override for specific records. we'll need clear instructions and we keep the logs tamper-evident.
[12:05] Speaker 6: (crosstalk)
[12:12] Alex: anything else on the SOC 2 deliverables?
[12:18] Maya: i'll attach the SOC2 Type II summary now, start the NDA exchange for full report. also i'll include the controls mapping for the parts of the platform we're using in the pilot.
[12:30] Priya: timeline check — after we get docs and SSO stable, we aim to do an in-region smoke test 9/22 and then decide on dedicated capacity commit. that tracks?
[12:40] Maya: yes that tracks.
[12:44] Mark: last question — are there any known gaps around ISO or FedRAMP that we should plan for?
[12:51] Liam: we don't currently have FedRAMP, but we do have customers running in regulated environments; ISO is in progress — i'll share status notes.
[13:05] Maya: ok, i'll recap next steps: send SOC2 attestation and KMS guide, liam to share audit log schema and sample digest, elmwood to confirm retention and provide test user. we'll queue the smoke test.
[13:20] Priya: thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[13:24] Maya: thanks all — i'll follow up with the docs and the cost estimate.

Recap / Next steps (verbatim):
- Maya: send SOC2 Type II summary + begin NDA for full report.
- Liam: upload audit-log NDJSON example + signed digest sample; share SSO checklist and runbook.
- Elmwood (Mark/Priya/Alex): confirm retention window (30 vs 90), provide test user and IdP details, confirm stakeholders for smoke test.

References shared in chat: 
- SSO checklist (link)
- KMS integration guide (link to doc)
- Audit log schema (ndjson example)

End of transcript.
